title: Moving to COD sets limits to $0 and keeps the old limit in the note
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, working in {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Net 30 is the shop's default for new customers.
  • The shop's own term {Term-A}, due 15 days after the invoice date, is held by exactly three customers, {Customer-A}, {Customer-B} and {Customer-C} (a new term holds only this case's customers), whose names are in that A to Z order, with credit limits of $500.00, $0.00 and $1,000.00.
    For example: {Term-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S4-13 N15, {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S4-13 Alpha, {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S4-13 Bravo and {Customer-C} is ZZAUTOTEST S4-13 Charlie.
  • Your user name is {User-A}.
    For example: {User-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S4-13 Admin.
  • Starting screen: the Credit Terms page (Settings, then "Credit Terms" in the Finance group) is open on the Active tab.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the "⋯" at the right of the {Term-A} row.
  2. Click "Move Customers".
  3. Choose "COD" in "Move To".
  4. Click "Move 3 Customers".
  5. Click "Set Limits To $0 And Move".
  6. Open {Customer-A}'s Notes tab.
  7. Open {Customer-B}'s Notes tab.
  8. Open {Customer-C}'s Notes tab.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the menu opens.
  • Step 2: a window titled "Move Customers from {Term-A}" opens.
  • Step 3: the $0 line shows.
  • Step 4: the confirmation opens.
  • Step 5: the window closes and the toast "3 customers moved to COD." shows.
  • Step 6: the note reads "Credit term changed from {Term-A} to COD by {User-A} (Move Customers). Credit limit $500.00 → $0." and the customer's credit limit is now $0.00.
  • Step 7: the note reads "Credit term changed from {Term-A} to COD by {User-A} (Move Customers)." with no credit-limit part (its limit was already $0.00).
  • Step 8: the note ends "Credit limit $1,000.00 → $0." and the limit is $0.00.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11673 (Story 4, Move Customers)

  • S4-R16: “On "Set Limits to $0 and Move", each moved customer's credit limit is set to $0 along with the term.”
  • S4-R20: “When a move changes a customer's limit (a limit above $0 set to $0), that customer's note (S4-R11) ends with "Credit limit {old limit} → $0." A customer whose limit was already $0 or blank gets the S4-R11 note without it.”
  • S4-E3: “Moving customers to COD or Credit Hold sets each moved customer's credit limit to $0 (S4-R16), whatever limit they had, and keeps the previous limit in each note (S4-R20). Moving customers off COD or Credit Hold to another term leaves their $0 limit as it is until someone enters a new one in Edit Customer.”
  • Key Decisions: “Moving customers to COD or Credit Hold sets their credit limits to $0 only after a confirmation, and keeps each previous limit in that customer's note.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Note on each moved customer | "Credit term changed from {old term} to {new term} by {user name} (Move Customers)." followed by "Credit limit {old limit} → $0." when the move changed the limit | Note on the customer's Notes”

From: Jira stories under epic SV-11638 (saved 23 Oct 2026, sources/JIRA-SV-11638-stories-2026-10-23.md), read 23 Oct 2026

  • Jira SV-11673 acceptance criterion: “Given a customer with a $500 limit moved to COD, then its limit is $0 and its note reads "Credit term changed from {old term} to COD by {user name} (Move Customers). Credit limit $500.00 → $0." (S4-R11, S4-R16, S4-R20).”
